original_card.question: Can one misleading historical-current claim or missing research cross-reference be corrected?
methods: Trace one confusing path from onboarding to its authoritative source.
Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Produce evidence-backed navigation, preserve historical records and avoid a duplicate global survey.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Repair one confusing path or produce a scoped map of one related obstruction family.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Clear navigation lowers entry cost for central research; a global survey without a concrete fix is not required.
allowed_variations: One historical-current ambiguity or one bounded family index.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting frozen scientific packages just to change their historical wording.

actual_scope: One bounded family index at three directions: what one array can hold in the output of a call shared with a second array, in the frame game (the engine game with its Pauli part dropped; terms in Sp(2m, 2), free elements the stabiliser of the raw frame, paid calls the transvections outside it). For two kinds of two-term part of one shared middle call at 3 address bits (10,752 free elements each), with coefficient 1, -1, 2 or 1/2 for the first kind and 1, -1 or 2 for the second, the package decides exactly whether one more call alone (no free step applied to its output) can finish the part, and whether a call that could be the other array's last call can have it removed. No tested part is both. For the first kind one rule fits every tested case (same frame: finishable exactly when 1 + c.g is invertible, removable exactly when it is not; other frames: neither); it is not proved. Two additions are checked: with a free step after the last call 128 more parts of the first kind are finished at coefficient 1 (512 at 2 and at 1/2), none of them removable; and the parts on adjacent frames are removable at coefficient +1 or -1 only by four calls that cannot be a last call. With one spare address bit (4 bits) the rule is checked on a seeded sample of 100 cases only. The open case (2 in 5 at three directions with one spare address bit, a saving of 1.66e-1 in the paid calls of one unit, not a kappa) is stated with its status and is not settled.
scope_change_reason: The card's method 'Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses' fits: the package ties one conflict that the hub met on examples in October (lee-phys's two-image prefix, #4688; JoyboyBrian's #4751 and #4797) to the statements in my repository, to the earlier bounds (eumemic's #288, Jose Manuel's #2108, my #4628) and to Dugongue's census of the same finite geometry (#4743), and names the open case. It is more than navigation because it also adds a result that is not on main: the table and the rule that describes its first kind of part. The game is stated in every claim.
bottleneck_link: A 2 in 5 at three directions with one spare address bit would save 1.66e-1 in the paid calls of one unit, and no bound I know excludes it. This package shows, for two kinds of two-term part of one shared call and the coefficients tested, which parts the last call alone can finish and which can be removed, and that none is both, which narrows where a search for that unit should look. It does not change kappa.
stop_rule: One table, its rule and its controls, rebuilt by verify.py in exact rational arithmetic; no search for the open case and no Lean build for this package.
evidence: verify.py, standard library, exact rational arithmetic, no file read or written; times with Python 3.12 on an Apple M4. --part main (about 38 s): at 3 address bits, for both kinds of part with coefficient 1 and all 10,752 free elements, the counts 9,983 tested / 769 plain in disguise / 128 finishable by the call alone / 639 removable by a call that could be a last call / 1,407 removable by any call that does not undo the shared call (kind A) and 9,984 / 768 / 0 / 128 / 128 (kind B), no case both, the kind A rule on every tested case, and the reduction to 1,632 classes tested directly on 80 cases. --part poststep (about 4 s): the kind A parts with frames further apart that one call and one free step on its output finish (128, 0, 512 and 512 for coefficients 1, -1, 2 and 1/2), each identity checked term by term. --part symmetry (about 42 s): the free elements carry the first call to each of the 56 calls; 768 symmetries carry one shared call to each of the 48 that give a level-2 term; the whole table again for a second shared call; the symmetry map tested on 368 distinct cases. --part coefficients (about 85 s): kind A with coefficients -1, 2 and 1/2 and kind B with -1 and 2, the kind A rule on every case, none both. --part spare (about 22 s): the rule on a seeded sample of 100 kind A parts at 4 address bits. --part controls (about 3 s): the solver finds the plain third call and refuses a target two calls away; arithmetic modulo 2^61 - 1 agrees on 92 seeded cases; three wrong variants of the rule are rejected. Not registered: --part full, every case one at a time with no symmetry reduction (run once in four quarters; same totals). Local only, not in this package: two AI reviewers' own programs, which rebuilt the counts of an earlier form of the table and between them found the two additions.
author: Jacob Sussman
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: I did this work with the help of AI agents (Anthropic's Claude). The programs, the searches, the arguments and the text were written by the agents under my direction. Two AI reviewers rebuilt the counts of an earlier form of this table from the definitions with their own programs, and between them found the two corrections of README section 5 (local only: those programs are not in this package). No independent human review of this package is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is there a 2 in 5 at three directions with one spare address bit (a saving of 1.66e-1 in the paid calls of one unit, not a kappa)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: In the engine game it is the smallest shape at three directions (fewest arrays, fewest calls) that no bound I know excludes; my best lower bound there is 2.4883 calls per array (checked by computer, by one family of programs) and the shape uses 2.5.
open_questions.first_step: The same arrangement (one call each, one shared call, one call each) at 4 address bits with every coefficient left free and the two last outputs read together; start with extra terms on the frame of the plain term, with kind B parts on adjacent frames, and with parts that a last call brings onto one frame.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing but size: 20,643,840 free elements at 4 address bits before any symmetry is used.

open_questions.question: Is the kind A rule a theorem at every number of address bits?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A proof by hand would replace the sample at 4 address bits and would say what a shared call can do at every block size.
open_questions.first_step: Show that a part whose two terms sit on different frames is never finishable by the call alone; the same-frame half is a statement about invertible elements of a group algebra.

open_questions.question: Why are exactly those 128 kind B parts removable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 128 are exactly the parts for which some call carries the plain term onto the frame of the extra term and the extra term onto the frame of the plain term, on all 9,984 cases, but I have no proof; a proof would complete the picture for two-term parts.
open_questions.first_step: Prove that such a call removes the part when the coefficient is +1 or -1.
